title: Help a person carry a pipe onto its stands, following their lead
instruction: Help the person lift the silver pipe onto the two pipe stands, then let go of it.
context: Pipefitters and plumbers (O*NET 47-2152.00) and construction laborers (47-2061.00) carry long pipe in pairs, and in a two-person lift one person leads while the other follows. A partner who lifts early, moves faster, keeps going when the leader stops or lets go on their own plan tips the load or pulls it out of the other's hands. The ability tested is leader-follower co-manipulation: matching a person's motion of a load you share, as they make it. Here a worker holds the far end of the pipe and leads at their own pace, which changes widely from trial to trial (when they lift, how fast they move and where they stop part way across), so no fixed timing works and the robot has to watch the person and follow their lead.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y to the robot's left). Pipe: silver aluminium tube, 25 mm outside diameter, 600 mm long, black plastic end caps, 300 g, with a red tape band 20 mm wide from x 68.5 to 70.5. It lies along x from x 14 to x 74 at y -9, its centre line 5.25 cm above the table, resting on two foam blocks. Foam blocks: two grey EVA foam blocks, 5 x 5 cm and 4 cm tall, about 10 g each, taped to the table at x 40 and x 66, y -9. Pipe stands: two orange steel pipe jack stands, about 1 kg each, clamped to the table at x 40 and x 66, y +9: four splayed legs, a round post with a height pin and a V-head of two 40 x 32 x 4 mm plates at 45 degrees, vertex 7.7 cm above the table, top edges 10 cm; a pipe resting in both heads has its centre line 9.5 cm above the table, 18 cm to the left of where it starts. Person: a worker in a hi-vis vest and hard hat stands across the table, past its far edge, and grips the far end of the pipe in their right hand (fist round x 70 to 74, by the red band). Once a gripper has held the pipe (within 15 mm of its centre line, anywhere from x 14 to x 63, opening 30 mm or less) for 1 s, the person waits 0.5 to 5 s, lifts their end 10 cm over 1 to 2.5 s, pauses 0.3 to 3 s, carries it 18 cm to the left over 2 to 5 s of movement with one stop of 0 to 3 s at 30 to 70 percent of the way, pauses 0.3 to 2 s, lowers it 5.75 cm into the stand heads over 0.8 to 2 s and keeps holding. Each of the eight draws comes from the trial seed; the person moves smoothly and never reacts to the robot. If the robot never takes hold, the person never lifts.
scoring: Measured every control step; the record (peak stretch and tilt, rungs reached, release time) is kept on every control step and cleared only when the simulator resets for a new trial, so putting the pipe back never clears it. Gates, checked first (either gives 0): the person's grip point on the pipe was ever more than 25 mm from their hand (they lose their grip), or the pipe ever pitched or yawed more than 4 degrees from level and straight (it tipped or swung). 0.25: at some step both pipe ends were at least 40 mm above their start height. 0.5: at some step both ends' centre line was at least 11 cm above the table with the pipe's centre at y +4.5 or more (carried over the stands). 0.75: at the end the pipe rests in both V-heads: its centre line within 5 mm of 9.5 cm above the table at both stands, its centre within 8 mm of y +9 and within 20 mm of x 44. 1.0: 0.75 and let go: both grippers' pads and centre points at least 30 mm from the pipe surface, both grippers and the pipe slower than 5 mm/s for the last 1 s, and the robot let go only after the person finished lowering. The robot has let go when no gripper holds the pipe and every gripper that held it has opened past 32 mm or moved 10 mm off it; a one-arm regrasp while the other gripper holds is not letting go. Letting go earlier caps the score at 0.75. Success when 1.0 holds for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the pipe back on the two foam blocks at its tape marks (x 14 to 74 cm, y -9 cm), red band at the person's end. The person takes hold at x 71 cm, steps back to their start mark and keeps their hand still at its start height until the robot has held the pipe for 1 s. Check that both stands are on their marks. The person's eight timing draws for the next trial come from its seed (partner_plan(seed) in task.py returns them).
fidelity: The person is a scripted rigid figure: the hand moves on two stiff slides and holds the pipe through a 3-axis grip spring (800 N/m) and bending springs (2 N m/rad) with free roll; they never react to the robot. Losing grip is judged at 25 mm of spring stretch, not simulated. The torso steps across with the hand but does not rise with it. Stands and foam are fixed. The 600 mm, 0.30 kg tube stands in for a 3 m pipe at tabletop scale.
